follow_ups: Ask for the reporting window and exact denominator of agent-created issues, plus app sessions and human-created work per existing active workspace. Separate more tracking activity from shipped changes and customer growth.

Track coding-session and Loops adoption, incremental retention and revenue, and gross margin after model tokens, sandbox runtime, support and unsuccessful runs. Use current [AI-credit terms](https://linear.app/docs/ai-credits), not an assumed API markup, when modelling economics.
Request enterprise wins attributable to the agent offering and the opportunity cost of delayed large-workspace features; the interview's shortlist effect is management interpretation.
Measure support tickets and severity per employee, resolution quality and human editing time before attributing avoided hiring to AI. Distinguish staffing growth restraint from workforce reductions.

Treat the $100 million ARR and 40,000 paying-customer figures as previously disclosed context: [Linear's August 26 announcement](https://linear.app/now/sharing-growth-with-the-people-building-linear) reported them before this episode. The title alone is not evidence of a fresh revenue milestone.

signals.claim: Cordova reports growing human-created work alongside agent-created issues exceeding half of Linear's total, and argues that native workflows and shared interfaces preserve the application's role.
signals.evidence: At 00:21:01 she says agents create over 50% of issues; at 00:21:24 and 00:22:37 she says work created within Linear's apps is also rising. She points to visualization and collaboration as reasons users return, and rejects relying only on a database behind an MCP server. Linear already reported a 50% agent-created work share in its [August 26 update](https://linear.app/now/sharing-growth-with-the-people-building-linear), so the threshold is not a newly disclosed breakthrough. The interview adds the simultaneous app-activity observation and commercial rationale; it provides no cohort-adjusted growth, completed-code measure or causal attribution.

signals.claim: Linear keeps seat subscriptions while adding usage charges for expensive agent work; Cordova says task-value ambiguity makes a uniform outcome fee unsuitable.
signals.evidence: She contrasts the variable value of bug triage with the variable cost of backlog queries and coding sessions. Most AI features remain included; coding sessions and Loops add consumption charges rather than replacing seats or charging for formerly free core features. Her API-cost-plus-a-small-addition description should not be read as current token markup: [Linear's AI-credit terms](https://linear.app/docs/ai-credits) specify provider-rate model tokens with no markup plus separately billed sandbox runtime, funded from a shared prepaid balance. The [August 20 pricing update](https://linear.app/changelog/2026-08-20-coding-environments) already separated those components. No AI revenue mix or gross margin is disclosed.

signals.claim: Cordova says Linear deferred planned enterprise features in 2025 to build its MCP server, agent APIs and coding-agent partnerships, betting that those would win enterprise consideration instead.
signals.evidence: These agent projects were absent from the beginning-of-2025 plan. She says the company did not simply deliver both roadmaps: some features for larger workspaces, including richer team and cross-team structures, were displaced. Her rationale was to lead the new development workflow, and she believes this put Linear on enterprise shortlists where it otherwise would not have appeared. That customer-acquisition effect is management's interpretation, without deal counts or a controlled comparison. At 01:01:13 she says the current product roadmap extends at most six months.

signals.claim: Cordova says AI-assisted support has reduced Linear's need to add staff while humans still review replies; she explicitly distinguishes that from downsizing.
signals.evidence: Linear keeps support in-house because it is often a customer's first human contact. AI can draft answers, but staff decide whether they are useful and concise instead of automatically sending a model answer first. When asked about cutting the team, she corrects the premise: she believes hiring has grown less than it would have without the tools. This is an operational design and a counterfactual staffing assessment, not evidence of layoffs or a measured support-productivity uplift; no headcount, ticket-volume or resolution-rate comparison is given.

summary: Linear COO Cristina Cordova explains how an established seat-priced application is adapting to agents: native orchestration and collaboration keep humans in the product, while costly coding and recurring agent work add usage revenue. She says agents create more than half of Linear issues while work created inside the app is also increasing. The useful additions are the operating choices behind that strategy: sacrificing planned enterprise features in 2025, retaining human review of AI-drafted support, and distinguishing core subscriptions from incremental AI consumption. Several headline milestones were already public; neither issue counts nor her staffing observations establish measured productivity gains.
why_it_matters: The interview offers a concrete case of an incumbent application trying to retain the customer relationship as agents take over workflow steps. Linear is funding that transition through a hybrid of seats and paid AI usage, while accepting roadmap trade-offs and preserving human quality control. The key questions are whether native workflows improve retention and completed work, and whether usage revenue covers the full cost of delivering them.
